
### ‘slots’  {.smaller}



* if packets take a fixed amount of time…
* want to wait whole number of packet times 

   * immediately after, one after, two after, three after

* avoids requiring almost 2 packets worth of ‘quiet’ time
* can synchronize by observing end of last transmission, or central clock

![](/multiaccess/texfig/carrier-sense-slots.figure.svg){width=1000px}


### carrier sense  {.smaller}


* channel can be ‘busy’ or not
* radio/light: 

   * have some sort of signal detectable on frequency
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* ‘‘carrier sense’’
* way to detect whether channel busy


### using carrier sense  {.smaller}


* simple idea: don't transmit if channel already busy 
<hr class="vspace" />
* problem: then when do you transmit?
* some options: 

   * never, lose the packet
   * immediately when it stops being busy
   * sometime after it stops being busy



### fixed-size frames, slots  {.smaller}


* ‘slotted’ Aloha
* challenge: synchronize everyone's timing
* then: everyone chooses slots to (re)transmit in
* but: not using carrier-sense before sending 

   * if everyone sync'd, not useful with fixed-size packets
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* requires 1-packet-unit empty periods
* 36% utilization (twice for naive version)


### exercise: slot timing  {.smaller}


* assume radio propogation at $2.9 \times 10^8$ m/s
* transmitting 1500-byte frames (including all headers, etc.) at 100 Mbit/sec
* over 5 km x 5 km area 
<hr class="vspace" />
* if we want slots that hold whole packet…
* how long should slots need to be?


### exercise solution 


* 1500-byte = 12000-bit @ 100Mbit/sec = 120 $\mu$s
* 5 km x 5 km $\rightarrow$ $\sim$ 7 km max distance
* 7000 m @ $2.9  \times 10^8$ m/s = 24 $\mu$s
* probably would need slot time around 140-150 $\mu$s?


### slots and variable-length packets  {.smaller}


* with variable-length packets + carrier-sense, slots still useful
* … but don't expect packets to occupy one slot 
<hr class="vspace" />
* idea: divide time up into slots
* slot time $\sim$ amount of time needed to detect transmission 

   * will depend on physical layer way to transmit packet bits

* don't transmit if detected non-ending transmission in previous slot


### exercise: variable length slot advantage  {.smaller}


* suppose we transmitting a 1000 $\mu$s packets
* use 10 $\mu$s slots 

   * and can reliably detect if a slot was occupied

* transmit algorithm: 

   * wait for network to be quiet for 1 slot
   * transmit in rand(0, $2^\text{attempts}$) slots

* two transmitters after previous packet --- expected time for next packet?


### 802.11b typical slots  {.smaller}


* $20 \mu\text{s}$ slots
* $50 \mu\text{s}$ interframe spacing (IFS) 

   * includes time to receive ACK of packet, switch from receive to xmit
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* transmit first time after IFS (if idle)
* transmit second time after IFS + rand($0$, $2^5$) slots 

   * plus time spent by other seen transmissions

* third time after rand($0$, $2^6$) slots, etc.


### 802.11b packet lengths  {.smaller}


* variable bit rate: max = 11Mbit
* approx 300--12000 bit frames 

   * = 27 to 1090 microseconds
 
<hr class="vspace" />
* do carrier sense before transmitting always
* different purpose for slots than slotted Aloha
